placementGuidelines.guideline: Position sofa as room focal point, typically facing media wall or fireplace. Maintain 12-18 inches clearance from walls for visual breathing room.
doExamples: Kent Sofa centered facing media wall with 15" wall clearance
Rialto Sofa positioned to maximize natural light from windows
Mitchell Sofa anchoring spacious 17.5x14.5 room
Melle Sofa scaled appropriately for compact 11.5x10 space
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Sofa is primary seating and visual anchor. Proper clearance allows for cleaning, prevents cramped feeling, and creates balanced proportions.

placementGuidelines.guideline: Place coffee table 14-18 inches from sofa front edge. Use round tables in tight spaces or to soften angular furniture.
doExamples: Bingham coffee table centered 16" from Kent Sofa
Zeno coffee table 15" from Rialto Sofa with side table access
Trula round coffee table softening geometry in Executive Suite
Caspian coffee table proportioned for compact 11.5x10 room
dontExamples: Coffee table too far (24"+) making reach difficult
Coffee table too close (<12") limiting leg room
placementGuidelines.reasoning: 14-18 inch distance allows comfortable reach without sacrificing leg room. Round tables improve flow in compact spaces.

placementGuidelines.guideline: Position side tables at sofa arm height or slightly lower. Place within easy reach for drinks and lighting.
doExamples: Chameau side table at Rialto Sofa arm for drinks and lamp
Dusk accent table beside Mitchell Sofa in Executive Suite
dontExamples: Side table too far from seating
Side table height mismatched to sofa arm
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Side tables provide functional surface within arm reach. Height alignment creates visual harmony and ergonomic comfort.

placementGuidelines.guideline: Place floor lamps in room corners or beside seating for ambient and task lighting. Maximum one floor lamp per room to avoid visual clutter.
doExamples: Colome floor lamp in corner between Kent Sofa and windows for balanced lighting
Fordham floor lamp providing task lighting for desk zone in multi-purpose room
dontExamples: Multiple floor lamps creating visual clutter
Floor lamp far from seating without purpose
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Floor lamps add ambient lighting and define zones. Corner placement maximizes space efficiency. One per room maintains clean aesthetic.

placementGuidelines.guideline: Use sectionals to maximize seating in compact spaces (under 15x11). Position to define conversation zone while maintaining traffic flow.
doExamples: Langham 3-piece sectional maximizing seating in 14.5x10 room
dontExamples: Sectional in oversized room (better served by sofa + chairs)
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Sectionals excel in compact rooms where separate sofa + chairs would overcrowd. Strategic placement defines zones without blocking flow.

placementGuidelines.guideline: Integrate storage (sideboards, bar cabinets) along walls to avoid interrupting conversation zones. Use as display and concealed storage.
doExamples: Hatch sideboard along wall in Executive Suite
Raffael bar cabinet wall-mounted in compact 11.5x10 room
Breya cabinet providing vertical storage in 14.5x10 sectional room
dontExamples: Cabinet in room center blocking flow
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Wall-positioned storage maximizes floor space while providing function. Keeps conversation zones open and maintains traffic flow.

placementGuidelines.guideline: In multi-purpose spaces (16x13+), define work zone separate from relaxation zone using furniture placement and lighting.
doExamples: Pilar desk with Ferris chair creating distinct work zone, Fordham floor lamp for task lighting, Hampton Sofa defining relaxation zone
dontExamples: Inadequate separation between work and living zones
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Clear zoning through furniture placement allows rooms to serve dual functions. Lighting reinforces zone separation.

placementGuidelines.guideline: Match furniture scale to room dimensions. Compact rooms (under 12x11) need streamlined pieces. Spacious rooms (17x14+) can accommodate substantial furniture.
doExamples: Streamlined Melle Sofa in compact 11.5x10 room
Substantial Mitchell Sofa in spacious 17.5x14.5 Executive Suite
Appropriately scaled collection in 14x11 Classic Comfort package
dontExamples: Undersized furniture lost in large room
Ignoring room dimensions in furniture selection
placementGuidelines.reasoning: Proper scale creates visual balance and functional comfort. Mismatched scale makes rooms feel cramped or empty.
